Our client seeks an experienced Group Compliance Officer to join their team and take senior compliance and financial crime accountability across the group's regulated entities. Subject to regulatory approval, this is a hands-on, senior position with direct ownership of the regulatory relationship with both the UK FCA and the IOM FSA, and a defining role in shaping the group's compliance framework as their fund platform widens. Key Responsibilities: Discharge statutory Compliance Officer role under Part 9 of the IOM Financial Services Rule Book. Maintain compliance monitoring programmes, regulatory returns, and statutory registers. Oversee SMF16 Compliance Oversight function, with ownership of AIFMD, MIFIDPRU, MAR, SYSC, and COBS compliance. Lead FCA supervisory dialogue, regulatory returns and notifications including AIFMD Annex IV reports. Hold MLRO function, managing group sanctions screening and customer due diligence. Run group AML/CFT programmes with particular attention to maritime risk factors. Provide regulatory advice on existing and new fund vehicles across multiple jurisdictions. Embed strong compliance culture across London, Isle of Man, Cyprus and Geneva operations. Report to relevant boards and committees on compliance and financial crime risk matters. Key Skills and Experience: Minimum three years compliance experience in regulated financial services. Working knowledge of IOM Financial Services Rule Book and AML/CFT Code 2019. Recognised compliance qualification such as ICA Diploma in Compliance or CISI Diploma in Investment Compliance. Strong working knowledge of FCA rules relevant to full-scope AIFMs including AIFMD, MIFIDPRU, MAR, SYSC, COBS. Direct prior experience as MLRO at a corporate service provider or comparable regulated entity would be desirable. maritime, shipping or commodities sector experience would be ideal. Evidence of ability to satisfy FCA fitness and propriety standards for SMF16 approval.

Altenar is a leading IT company founded in 2011 and headquartered in the Isle of Man, with offices in Malta, Greece, Georgia, Brazil and Uruguay.
We are seeking a proactive and detail oriented Junior Legal/Contracts Officer to support the legal, contracts, and governance functions of the business.
Key Responsibilities:
Assisting with the corporate governance of the Altenar group of Companies, including arranging board meetings and preparing agendas and board packs.
Assisting with the creation and preparation of documents for presentation to the Board of Directors for review and signature, particularly customer onboarding documentation.
Attending board meetings to assist with the recording and preparation of accurate board minutes.
Working with the Contracts Manager to ensure legal documents progress efficiently from drafting and collaboration (with all relevant stakeholders) through negotiation to  execution.
Ensuring physical and electronic filing is completed promptly and accurately, including  maintaining internal document databases and records.
Assisting the Compliance department with customer and supplier on-boarding processes.
Supporting general company administration, including insurance and data protection renewals and other corporate administrative requirements as they  arise. 
Assisting with banking administration and payment processes, as required.
Providing general administrative and ad-hoc business support as required from time to time.

Essential Requirements:
Good standard of general education, including GCSEs (or equivalent) in English and Maths.
Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.
Strong organisational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and competing priorities.
Strong written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills.
Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion and professionalism.
Proactive and self motivated approach, with the ability to work independently and take ownership of tasks.
Willingness and aptitude to learn new processes, systems, and areas of the business.
Ability to follow instruction carefully while also using initiative and sound judgement

Desirable Requirements:
Previous experience in an administrative, governance, legal support, compliance or company secretarial role, including exposure to board meetings or governance processes
Experience working within a regulated industry or professional services environment.
Familiarity with legal documentation, contracts administration, or compliance processes.
Experience maintaining document management systems or internal databases.
Understanding of customer and supplier onboarding processes.
Knowledge of data protection requirements and general corporate administration.

You will lead client meetings, deepen existing relationships, identify cross-selling opportunities and deliver new business, maintaining accurate pipeline records to support timely management information reporting. The ideal candidate will bring a minimum of 15 years' experience in the financial services industry, with proven expertise in trust and company administration. You will be a confident, polished communicator, commercially astute, highly organised and an ambassador for the business in every client interaction.

Notes
Our client seeks a commercially minded Legal Counsel to join their in-house team. Role Profile: This role offers the opportunity to take ownership of legal matters, work closely with the business, and play a hands-on role in shaping how legal supports a growing international company. This position is suited to a proactive and detail-oriented lawyer who is comfortable working independently, taking accountability, and driving continuous improvement in legal processes and documentation. Key responsibilities: Draft, review, and negotiate a wide range of commercial agreements, including SaaS/software licensing, partnerships, and supplier contracts. Act as a key legal contact for business stakeholders, providing clear, pragmatic, and commercially focused advice. Take ownership of legal support for designated business areas. Identify and implement improvements to legal processes, workflows, and ways of working. Develop and maintain contract templates, playbooks, and internal guidance. Collaborate with a multi-jurisdictional legal team. Manage external counsel and support disputes where required. Monitor relevant legal and regulatory developments in the gaming and technology sectors. Support strategic business initiatives, including new product development. Key Skills & Experience: 4-6 years PQE (post qualification experience) as a solicitor, advocate or equivalent required - this is a guideline so if you feel that you are suitable, please still apply. Strong grounding in commercial and contract law. Experience in the gaming industry/software development industry is advantageous but not essential. Ability to work independently, take ownership, and manage priorities. Experience improving legal processes, templates, or ways of working is highly desirable. Excellent drafting, negotiation, and communication skills. Ability to provide practical, business-focused advice in a clear and concise manner. Strong relationship-building skills and the ability to work effectively across different jurisdictions and cultures. A proactive, solutions-oriented mindset and interest in the gaming/technology space. Experience working with legal technology tools (e.g. CLM systems, document automation) is advantageous. Interest in leveraging AI and legal technology to improve legal service delivery and efficiency is desirable. 
 If you have the required skills please apply online at searchandselect.com quoting reference number: 16633

Main Responsibilities:
Continuously assess the needs of children, young people, and their parents; supporting a multi-agency approach to assessment and planning. 
Work in a variety of settings, in particular the home environment, to develop realistic and achievable action plans, in consultation with children, young people and their parents, which are based on their assessed needs and written in a way that is easy for them to understand.
Agree targets, in consultation parents and children, and monitor, evaluate and measure progress against them. Capture evidence of the distance travelled in terms of positive changes, using the Family Star (outcomes measurement tool). 

Main Requirements (for details check the job description and person specification):
NVQ Level 3 or equivalent qualification or experience in Health, Childcare, Social care; or other relevant qualification.
Demonstrated experience of working with and supporting children and families, including experience of working within the family home and community settings.
Good knowledge of safeguarding children practice, and the importance of working within relevant policies and procedures.
Appointments are subject to Family Action receiving a satisfactory disclosure from the Disclosure and Barring Service – Enhanced with Children’s Barred List.

Benefits: 
an annual paid leave entitlement that commences at 25 working days, and after a full year of service, rising each April by one day, subject to a maximum of 30 working days plus bank holidays.
up to 6% matched-pension contributions.
enhanced paid sick leave and paid family leave provisions.
eye care and winter flu jabs vouchers.
cycle to work scheme.
investing in your professional development with ongoing quality training and career development opportunities.

In this role, you will lead cross-functional projects within the Group change portfolio, working closely with colleagues, stakeholders and third-party partners to deliver outcomes through structured project management and Agile delivery practices.
Leading cross-functional projects from initiation through to implementation, ensuring delivery of business value on time, within budget and to agreed quality standards.
Managing a varied portfolio of change, including digital and technology initiatives, regulatory programmes, operational improvements, and new products or market opportunities.
Applying strong project governance alongside Agile delivery disciplines, including planning, sprint oversight, issue and risk management, reporting and budget control.
Partnering with stakeholders to shape requirements, prioritise delivery and ensure solutions meet customer, business and regulatory needs.
Supporting iterative delivery through effective scope management, testing coordination, release readiness and continuous improvement.
Facilitating clear, consistent communication across project teams, sponsors and stakeholders to maintain alignment and momentum.
Helping teams and business areas adapt to change by embedding new ways of working and supporting successful adoption. 
Requirements for the role 	
At least three years’ project management experience, ideally within Financial Services, although this is not essential.
Hands-on experience working in Agile and Scrum environments, ideally delivering digital, technology or business change initiatives with internal and third-party teams.
Strong project delivery skills, including planning, governance, issue and risk management, reporting, budget oversight and delivering incremental value.
Confidence leading complex projects or multiple workstreams at once, with the ability to balance pace, control and delivery quality.
The ability to build trusted relationships with delivery teams, product owners, senior stakeholders, third parties and outsource providers.
Clear facilitation, presentation and report-writing skills.
A collaborative, practical mindset with the confidence to guide teams through ambiguity, remove delivery blockers and support continuous improvement.
Strong knowledge of Agile and Scrum principles, with PRINCE2, Scrum certification or an equivalent project management qualification desirable.
Flexibility to travel where a project requires it, including overseas if needed.

For more details and to apply contact careers@ifg-ltd.com

Council Advocate

Grade: Principal Officer, SCP 40 – 46 (£59,456 - £68,607)

The Council invites applications from highly motivated Manx qualified advocates to join our team. Working with our existing Council Advocate you’ll deliver a fast paced, effective and efficient in-house legal service.

From supporting housing, property, regulatory and contract work to providing comprehensive legal advice and guidance across the organisation to tackling litigation matters representing the Council in courts and tribunals and navigating the local government arena, the range of legal work is diverse, dynamic and challenging.

Working closely with the Chief Executive and the Corporate Management Team you will also collaborate with senior officers and Members of Council for work that is anything but routine.

For the right person, this role offers meaningful responsibility, backed by the Council’s commitment to development and continuous improvement in service delivery. In-house local government practice is varied and exciting, with opportunities beyond traditional legal duties that stretch beyond the ordinary.

Ambitious? Dedicated to delivering exceptional service? We WANT you – whether you’re newly qualified, returning to work after a break or seeking a fresh challenge. Apply now by heading to our Job Train portal via the Council’s website. Questions - contact HR (hr@douglas.gov.im) on 01624 696455.

For an informal chat about the role, contact Jan Keig, Executive Officer (01624 696319) to arrange a call with Kathy Rice, Chief Executive.

Environment & Regeneration Department – Dilapidation Enforcement Officer.
Grade 6, SCP 24 – 30 (£37,374 – £45,313).

We are seeking a motivated and proactive Dilapidation Enforcement Officer to join our Environment and Regeneration Department and play a key role in helping to maintain and improve the appearance, safety and amenity of the City.

This varied role will involve dealing with dangerous structures, dilapidated and unsightly properties, using a combination of advice, negotiation and enforcement action to ensure buildings and land are brought back to an acceptable condition. You will be a key point of contact for property-related enforcement matters, liaising with owners, members of the public, emergency services, contractors, consultants and other agencies.

The post will also support the Council’s town planning functions, including reviewing planning applications, preparing reports and contributing to the Council’s wider Cleaner, Safer, Greener agenda. The successful candidate will have strong communication and organisational skills, the ability to interpret legislation and technical information, and the confidence to make informed decisions in a busy and varied working environment.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with an interest in property, planning, enforcement or regeneration to make a visible contribution to the City and support improvements that benefit residents, businesses and visitors.

Apply now by heading to our Job Train portal via the Council’s website. For an informal chat about the role please contact Alan Gordon, Community & Enforcement Manager on 696326 or by email at agordon@douglas.gov.im.  Alternatively, you can contact the Human Resources Section on 696455. 

Closing date for submission of applications is Friday 17th July 2026 at 5.00 pm.

Our client seeks a talented Data/BI Analyst to join their team for a 12-month contract. You'll play a key role in transforming data into meaningful business insights. You'll work closely with stakeholders across the organisation to understand business challenges, build impactful dashboards and reports, and develop data-driven solutions that support strategic decision-making. This is an exciting opportunity for someone who enjoys combining technical expertise with business engagement. You'll be responsible for data modelling, data quality management, reporting and analytics, while helping to build and enhance the organisation's data capabilities. Key Responsibilities: Establish and manage key data management competencies such as data quality assurance, metadata management, master data management, and data modelling. Support data governance and control frameworks to maintain data quality and data integrity. Document and maintain source-to-target mappings, data flows, and data definitions. Design and facilitate user self-service of tactical data requests and report working with data analysts and business users. Engage with business stakeholders to understand their requirements, translating these into actionable data insights, dashboards, and reports. Re-engineer manual data flows for scalability and improved efficiency in reporting, working with other departments. Build the advanced analytics capability using tools such as Python, PySpark, Machine Learning utilising statistical data techniques. Monitor team workflows, resource allocation, and project progress, while ensuring team members' professional development through training and development. Key Skills and Experience: Proven experience in a Data Analyst/Business Analyst (data focused), or similar role. Data modelling experience. Advanced data visualisation and report creation skills (Power BI reports and dashboards). Advanced working knowledge of Microsoft Excel. Data cleansing and data enrichment experience. Advanced knowledge of SQL data queries and joins. Knowledge and experience in data governance. Excellent communication skills, communicating between technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Notes
Environment & Regeneration Department - City Warden
 
Grade 4, SCP 16 – 22 (£29,731 - £ 35,225)
37-hour week plus contractual overtime (8 hr 10 min weekly). Includes weekend, working 1 in 3.
 
We are looking for a highly motivated individual to take on the role of City Warden.  You will be required to provide excellent customer service to the residents of Douglas, the City centre visitors, users of the Council’s car parks and patrol areas, as directed, on a daily basis.  The role includes improving the experience of Douglas using initiatives and enforcement to deter environmental offences as well as inspecting Council facilities and equipment (e.g., lifebelts, B-lines life-saving equipment) and ensuring care for the environment by carrying out street-scene activities.

About the role- You will work onsite and report into the Assistant or Store Manager and your role could be to help on the tills, advise our customers, or work in our back shop. 
You will also: 
Help our customers and put them at ease; whether that’s listening to find out more about them, answering questions and giving great advice on our fantastic products, recommending items they hadn’t considered or simply offering a basket - it's the little things that make a difference. 
Get to know our in-store offers and schemes and promote them - the more info we can give our customers the better. 
Help our stores run smoothly - this could look like ensuring we have the right products displayed on the shop floor, providing a great service on our tills, or helping with our stock in in the stock rooms. 
Work with other members in the team to provide a great shopping experience, ensuring the store is always clean and presentable to provide a store everyone can be proud of. You will be provided with award winning training accredited by the Institute of Customer Service.
What you’ll need to have- These are the essential skills or experience needed to succeed in this role: Full training is provided for this role, and we are looking for people who:
Excel in a varied environment, working at pace. 
Communicate and listen effectively. 
Enjoy working as part of a team, promoting a collaborative team dynamic.
Know that the little things make the biggest difference for customer interactions. 
Desire to be a proud brand ambassador for Boots and help our customers find the best products for them. 
Our benefits- 
Boots Retirement Savings Plan. Discretionary annual bonus. Generous employee discounts. Enhanced maternity/paternity/adoption leave pay and gift card for anyone expecting or adopting a child. Flexible benefits scheme. Access to free, 24/7 counselling and support through TELUS Health, our Employee Assistance Programme. 
We have a great range of benefits in addition to the above that offer flexibility to suit you - find out more at boots.jobs/rewards. Please note, any salary estimates given on third-party sites are not provided or endorsed by Boots and may not be accurate. 
Why Boots?
 At Boots, we foster a working environment where consideration and inclusivity help everyone to be themselves and reach their full potential. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, passionate about embracing the diversity of our colleagues and providing a positive and inclusive working environment for all. As the heart of everything we do at Boots, it's with you, we change for the better. 
What's next? 
If your application is successful, you will be invited to attend an in-store interview within the next 14 days.
Apply online at boots.jobs ref- 275908BR

Notes
Are you someone who enjoys hands-on work, thrives in a laboratory environment, and takes pride in doing things with accuracy and care? We’re looking for a Production Technician to join our team and play a key role in manufacturing high-quality chromatography products that support important scientific and commercial outcomes.

This is more than just a production role — it’s an opportunity to contribute to continuous improvement, process optimisation, and innovation in a regulated, high-performing environment.
This role will be a Fixed Term Contract.
You’ll be at the heart of our manufacturing operations, helping ensure our products are produced safely, efficiently, and to the highest standards. Your responsibilities will include - Manufacturing chromatography products, intermediates, and base materials - Following established SOPs and production methods with precision - Recording production data accurately and maintaining detailed documentation - Carrying out on-line quality control checks and identifying any anomalies early - Supporting process optimisation and improvement initiatives - Maintaining equipment and ensuring a clean, safe working environment. 
You’ll also contribute to - Improving processes and maximising yields - Writing and updating SOPs and production methods - Sharing knowledge and supporting the development of colleagues. 
We’re looking for someone who is practical, detail-focused, and proactive, with a genuine interest in laboratory-based manufacturing.
You’ll thrive in this role if you are - A strong team player with good communication skills - Highly organised with excellent attention to detail - 
Comfortable working both independently and as part of a team - A natural problem solver who can spot issues early - Able to follow processes accurately while also contributing ideas for improvement. 
Desirable experience - Degree in a scientific discipline - Experience in regulated manufacturing (ideally chemical or similar environments) - Familiarity with laboratory equipment and processes. 
This is a hands-on, laboratory-based role where no two days are quite the same. You can expect - A physically active role involving standing, lifting, and equipment operation - A structured environment with a strong focus on quality and safety - 24/7 shift patterns supporting continuous operations
To Apply please follow this link - https://biotage-1708019070.teamtailor.com/jobs/7453461-production-chemist-astrea-bioseparations-fixed-term-contract
